_comment: 🔮️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform. ISO 10303-214 CC5 (faceted B-Rep) is a validation-gated dialect over the SAME StepSnapshot the ✳️any subset owns, so it shares the snapshot type — but NOT the vocabulary: ✳️any declares the ISO 10303-21 grammar (insert-entity, set-entity-arg, …), while this catalog declares one kind per axis `check_cc5_conformance` actually reads. CC5's ceiling is FACETED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION; exactly one classified type, ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION, is out of reach, and it is the type the real committed export carries at #13 — the narrowest miss on the ladder. The ladder classification the oracle uses is re-derived from ISO 10303-214 §4.3 in ../../../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs, shared by all seven ap214 subsets so no class copies it, and never called out of the production `engine::ladder` — an oracle that asked the code under test how to classify would compare an implementation with itself. This subset declares no comparisonProfiles of its own: `semantic-step-conformance-class-v1` is declared once, in ../../✳️cc1/🧪️oracle/🔣️component.json, and the registry aggregator merges every discovered manifest repo-wide.

oracles.rationale: ruststep 0.4 is the real, independent ISO 10303-21 READER for this subset: `ast::Exchange::from_str` parses the real committed `📐️hexagonal-cut-concrete-forest-left-ap214.stp` (a genuine Rhino 8.31 / ST-Developer v19.2 export, 1,396 real entities) with zero errors, and it is what reads back every result this subset's oracle produces before `semantic-step-conformance-class-v1` compares it. It has NO writer at all (`ast::ser::to_record` only builds an in-memory `Record` from an already-typed struct; no `Display`/`fmt::Formatter` impl exists on `Exchange`/`DataSection`/`Record`/`Parameter`), so per the fleet brief's §6 nothing in this case is typed `@mode-differential` — ruststep cannot be a second PRODUCER of mutated bytes. The re-serializer is this standard's own from-scratch Part-21 writer in ../../../🧪️oracle/🦀️component.rs, deliberately independent of this repository's production `step::engine::part21` writer. What the evidence therefore is, stated plainly: a real third-party parse of the conformance-relevant STRUCTURE of every result — the ladder census, the declared schema and the product identity chain — plus the inverse and identity laws asserted in role, not a byte-level differential claim.
